summary: Sample Company sells autonomous mooring arms to mid-size ports. The team is credible and two paid pilots are live; the unit economics are unproven at seed.

sources.title: Port Technology International: Harbor pilots at Savannah

openItems.text: Confirm the Savannah pilot converts to a paid contract

verdict.reason: Two paid pilots and a founder who ran automation at a top-10 port meet the seed bar [^deck].
decidedBy: Founder ran terminal automation at the Port of Rotterdam for six years
Two paid pilots, one at Savannah [^press]
Labour shortages make the timing now

body.stageBar: Stage: seed. Reasonable evidence at this stage: product in market, first paid pilots, early retention. Not reasonable to expect: cohort economics or a sales team.

criteria.name: Team and founders
criteria.reasoning: CEO ran terminal automation at a top-10 port; CTO shipped industrial arms at a robotics firm.

criteria.name: Market opportunity
criteria.reasoning: Bottom-up sizing covers 310 mid-size ports; the TAM slide is top-down only.

criteria.name: Traction and validation
criteria.reasoning: Two paid pilots; no renewals yet.

criteria.name: Business model and unit economics
criteria.reasoning: Pilot pricing and hardware cost per unit are not in the materials; a unit cost sheet would resolve it.

highlights: Operator founder with direct port experience

founders.name: Maya Chen
founders.history: Head of terminal automation, Port of Rotterdam, 2018 to 2024. **Verified** by Apollo and the company site.
founders.gap: Why leave a senior port role? Ask on the call.

founders.name: Luis Ortega
founders.history: Robotics lead at an industrial arm maker, per the deck only.

body.foundersNote: Complementary: operations and robotics. Reference targets: the Rotterdam automation director; the Savannah pilot sponsor.

inconsistencies: Use of funds hires 9 engineers; the hiring plan slide shows 6.

research.findings: Savannah pilot confirmed by trade press in August 2026 [^press].

questions.question: What does the Savannah pilot cost you per arm, and what do they pay?
questions.why: Resolves business model, currently not assessed.

questions.question: What is the conversion path from pilot to fleet contract?
Which competitors have ports evaluated alongside you?
questions.why: The deck has no competition slide.
